# Billr MCP tools

<!-- Generated by app/scripts/generate-plugin-tool-reference.mjs. Do not edit. -->

Every tool the Billr MCP server registers: 53 of them, in the
groups the app itself uses. Titles, descriptions and inputs come straight
from the registered tool contracts, so nothing here can advertise a tool
that does not exist.

The **Needs** column is the permission the connection must have been
granted. A tool you cannot see was not granted; say so rather than working
around it.

`request_id` appears on write tools for idempotency: generate a fresh UUID
per intended operation, and reuse the same one with identical input when
retrying a call that may have half landed.

## Task billing

Track active work and reported usage under human-approved pricing.

| Tool | Needs | Required input |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `list_billing_policies` | read | none |
| `create_task` | write | `request_id`, `policy_id`, `title` |
| `start_task` | write | `request_id`, `task_id` |
| `heartbeat_task` | write | `request_id`, `task_id` |
| `pause_task` | write | `request_id`, `task_id` |
| `complete_task` | write | `request_id`, `task_id` |
| `record_task_usage` | write | `request_id`, `task_id`, `provider`, `provider_request_id`, `cost`, `currency`, `source` |
| `get_task_billing_preview` | read | `task_id` |

### `list_billing_policies`

*List Approved Pricing*, needs **read**.

Read human-approved task rates, usage multipliers, currencies and budgets. Agents cannot approve pricing.

- Required: nothing
- Optional: `business_id`

### `create_task`

*create task*, needs **write**.

Create a paused task using a human-approved pricing policy. A task has its own budget. Then start_task when active work begins.

- Required: `request_id`, `policy_id`, `title`
- Optional: `business_id`

### `start_task`

*start task*, needs **write**.

Start or resume active work. Send heartbeat_task every 30 to 60 seconds. Only the first 120 seconds after a heartbeat count; waiting for a user should be paused.

- Required: `request_id`, `task_id`
- Optional: `business_id`

### `heartbeat_task`

*heartbeat task*, needs **write**.

Record active elapsed time using server timestamps, capped at 120 seconds since the previous heartbeat. Retry with the same request ID to avoid counting twice.

- Required: `request_id`, `task_id`
- Optional: `business_id`

### `pause_task`

*pause task*, needs **write**.

Stop charging time while waiting or idle. Records up to 120 seconds since the last heartbeat.

- Required: `request_id`, `task_id`
- Optional: `business_id`

### `complete_task`

*complete task*, needs **write**.

Finish a task after logging all usage. Stops time and freezes work for human billing review. This cannot be undone.

- Required: `request_id`, `task_id`
- Optional: `business_id`

### `record_task_usage`

*record task usage*, needs **write**.

Record a known provider cost in the policy currency, with a unique provider request reference and evidence source. This is reported cost, not independently verified by Billr. Do not invent prices or submit estimates. Log before completing the task.

- Required: `request_id`, `task_id`, `provider`, `provider_request_id`, `cost`, `currency`, `source`
- Optional: `business_id`, `model`, `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`

### `get_task_billing_preview`

*Task Billing Preview*, needs **read**.

Read recorded active seconds and reported usage. Time excludes unrecorded running intervals. Completion and human approval are required before invoicing. Amounts are rounded per component.

- Required: `task_id`
- Optional: `business_id`

## Clients

Look up and maintain the client list.

| Tool | Needs | Required input |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `list_clients` | read | none |
| `get_client` | read | `client_id` |
| `create_client` | write | `name` |
| `update_client` | write | `client_id` |

### `list_clients`

*List Clients*, needs **read**.

List clients for one of the caller's businesses, ordered by name. Optionally filter by a case-insensitive substring search on name or email.

- Required: nothing
- Optional: `offset`, `business_id`, `search`

### `get_client`

*Get Client*, needs **read**.

Fetch full details for one client, including their five most recent invoices. The client must belong to one of the caller's businesses.

- Required: `client_id`
- Optional: nothing

### `create_client`

*Create Client*, needs **write**.

Create a new client under one of the caller's businesses. Fails with an instructive error if a client with the same name already exists in that business. Use update_client instead in that case.

- Required: `name`
- Optional: `business_id`, `email`, `phone`, `address_line1`, `address_line2`, `city`, `state`, `postal_code`, `country`, `currency`, `notes`

### `update_client`

*Update Client*, needs **write**.

Update fields on an existing client. Only fields provided are changed; omitted fields are left as-is. The client must belong to one of the caller's businesses.

- Required: `client_id`
- Optional: `name`, `email`, `phone`, `address_line1`, `address_line2`, `city`, `state`, `postal_code`, `country`, `currency`, `notes`

## Invoices

Draft, edit, send, and settle invoices.

| Tool | Needs | Required input |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `list_invoices` | read | none |
| `get_invoice` | read | none |
| `create_invoice` | write | `request_id` |
| `update_draft_invoice` | write | `invoice_id` |
| `send_invoice` | send | `request_id`, `invoice_id` |
| `record_payment` | payments | `request_id`, `invoice_id`, `amount` |

### `list_invoices`

*List Invoices*, needs **read**.

List invoices for the caller's businesses, most recent first. Optionally filter by business, status (including the synthetic 'unpaid' status, which matches sent/viewed/partial/overdue), and/or client.

- Required: nothing
- Optional: `offset`, `business_id`, `status`, `client_id`, `limit`

### `get_invoice`

*Get Invoice*, needs **read**.

Fetch full details for one invoice, including line items, client, and public/PDF links. Identify the invoice by invoice_id, or by invoice_number (optionally scoped to a specific business if the caller has more than one).

- Required: nothing
- Optional: `invoice_id`, `invoice_number`, `business_id`

### `create_invoice`

*Create Invoice*, needs **write**.

Draft a new invoice for a client, identified by client_id or client_name (exact match, case-insensitive). Always created as a draft. Use send_invoice separately to send it. Pass engagement_entry_ids to bill agreed work off an engagement schedule, which marks those entries invoiced in the same step so they can never be billed twice.

- Required: `request_id`
- Optional: `currency`, `business_id`, `client_id`, `client_name`, `line_items`, `issue_date`, `due_date`, `notes`, `status`, `time_entry_ids`, `expense_ids`, `engagement_entry_ids`, `discount_type`, `discount_value`, `tax_rate`, `shipping_amount`

### `update_draft_invoice`

*Update Draft Invoice*, needs **write**.

Update a draft invoice: replace its line items and/or adjust dates, notes, discount, tax, or shipping. Refuses to modify invoices that are no longer in draft status. Cancel and recreate instead.

- Required: `invoice_id`
- Optional: `line_items`, `notes`, `issue_date`, `due_date`, `discount_type`, `discount_value`, `tax_rate`, `shipping_amount`

### `send_invoice`

*Send Invoice*, needs **send (puts a document in front of a client)**.

Email an invoice (with PDF attached) to its client, advancing a draft to "sent"; defaults the recipient to the client's own email if `to` is omitted. Refuses to send invoices that are already paid or cancelled.

- Required: `request_id`, `invoice_id`
- Optional: `to`, `cc`, `bcc`, `subject`, `message`

### `record_payment`

*Record Payment*, needs **payments (moves recorded money)**.

Record a payment received against an invoice, updating the invoice's amount_paid/balance_due and status ("paid" once the balance reaches zero, "partial" otherwise). Mirrors the app's own Record Payment flow.

- Required: `request_id`, `invoice_id`, `amount`
- Optional: `payment_date`, `method`, `notes`, `reference_number`

## Estimates

Quote work up front, then turn an accepted quote into an invoice.

| Tool | Needs | Required input |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `list_estimates` | read | none |
| `get_estimate` | read | `estimate_id` |
| `create_estimate` | write | `request_id`, `line_items` |
| `update_draft_estimate` | write | `estimate_id` |
| `send_estimate` | send | `request_id`, `estimate_id` |
| `convert_estimate_to_invoice` | write | `estimate_id` |

### `list_estimates`

*List Estimates*, needs **read**.

List estimates (quotes) for the caller's businesses, most recent first, optionally filtered by business, status, or client. Use this to answer "what quotes are outstanding". Estimates are NOT invoices and never carry a balance; use list_invoices for anything about money owed.

- Required: nothing
- Optional: `offset`, `business_id`, `status`, `client_id`, `limit`

### `get_estimate`

*Get Estimate*, needs **read**.

Fetch one estimate in full: line items, totals, client, status, and the shareable link. Use it before update_draft_estimate or convert_estimate_to_invoice so you are editing the real current contents rather than assumed ones. It does not return payment or balance information, because an estimate is not an invoice; use get_payment_status for money owed.

- Required: `estimate_id`
- Optional: nothing

### `create_estimate`

*Create Estimate*, needs **write**.

Draft a new estimate (quote) for a client, identified by client_id or client_name. Use this when work has not been agreed yet and the client needs a price first. Always created as a draft: call send_estimate to deliver it, then convert_estimate_to_invoice once it is accepted. Do NOT use this for work already delivered; create_invoice is the right tool there.

- Required: `request_id`, `line_items`
- Optional: `business_id`, `client_id`, `client_name`, `issue_date`, `expiry_date`, `notes`, `terms`, `discount_type`, `discount_value`, `tax_rate`, `shipping_amount`

### `update_draft_estimate`

*Update Draft Estimate*, needs **write**.

Update a draft estimate: replace its line items and/or adjust dates, notes, terms, discount, tax, or shipping. Refuses to touch an estimate that has already been sent, accepted, declined, or converted, because the client has seen those numbers; create a new estimate instead.

- Required: `estimate_id`
- Optional: `line_items`, `issue_date`, `expiry_date`, `notes`, `terms`, `discount_type`, `discount_value`, `tax_rate`, `shipping_amount`

### `send_estimate`

*Send Estimate*, needs **send (puts a document in front of a client)**.

Email an estimate to its client and advance a draft to "sent". Defaults the recipient to the client's own email. Use it once the quote is final; it does not create an invoice and takes no payment. Refuses estimates that were already converted to an invoice.

- Required: `request_id`, `estimate_id`
- Optional: `to`, `cc`, `bcc`, `subject`, `message`

### `convert_estimate_to_invoice`

*Convert Estimate to Invoice*, needs **write**.

Turn an estimate into a draft invoice carrying the same line items, currency, notes, and terms, then mark the estimate "converted" and link the two. Use it once the client has agreed. It does NOT send the invoice; call send_invoice after. Refuses an estimate that was already converted, declined, or expired.

- Required: `estimate_id`
- Optional: `issue_date`, `due_date`

## Engagements

Agreed totals billed off a schedule, with nothing sent automatically.

| Tool | Needs | Required input |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `list_engagements` | read | none |
| `get_engagement` | read | `engagement_id` |
| `list_ready_to_bill` | read | none |
| `create_engagement` | write | `request_id`, `name`, `total`, `billing_mode` |
| `update_engagement` | write | `request_id`, `engagement_id` |
| `mark_milestone_complete` | write | `request_id`, `entry_id` |
| `complete_engagement` | write | `request_id`, `engagement_id` |
| `waive_engagement_entry` | write | `request_id`, `entry_id`, `reason` |
| `convert_estimate_to_engagement` | write | `request_id`, `estimate_id`, `billing_mode` |

### `list_engagements`

*List Engagements*, needs **read**.

List engagements: agreed pieces of work with a total and a payment schedule, for example "12,000 for the website rebuild, 50% up front and 50% on delivery". Use this to answer "what have we agreed with this client" or "what is still unbilled on this project". Each one reports how much has been billed, how much is left, and how many schedule entries are ready to bill now. Read-only, and nothing in the engagement tools ever sends anything to a client.

- Required: nothing
- Optional: `offset`, `business_id`, `client_id`, `status`, `has_ready_to_bill`, `limit`

### `get_engagement`

*Get Engagement*, needs **read**.

Read one engagement in full: the agreed total, what has been billed, what is left, and every schedule entry with its status, its due rule and the invoice it became. Use this before billing anything, so you bill the entries that are ready and not the ones that are already invoiced. Read-only, and nothing is sent to anyone.

- Required: `engagement_id`
- Optional: nothing

### `list_ready_to_bill`

*List Ready to Bill*, needs **read**.

List every engagement schedule entry that is ready to bill right now, across all clients. This is the "what should I invoice today" list: deposits on engagements that have started, milestones marked complete, dated payments whose date has passed, and final payments on completed engagements. Nothing here has been invoiced yet, and nothing is sent to anyone by looking. Read-only.

- Required: nothing
- Optional: `offset`, `business_id`, `client_id`, `limit`

### `create_engagement`

*Create Engagement*, needs **write**.

Record an agreed piece of work with a total and a payment schedule, for example "12,000 for the rebuild, 50% deposit and 50% on delivery" or "9,000 in 3 equal installments". The schedule is worked out on the server so the entries always add up to exactly the total; the last entry absorbs any rounding. Nothing is billed and nothing is sent by creating one: entries become ready to bill as their due rules fire, and you then raise an invoice for them. Use create_estimate instead when the price has not been agreed yet, and create_invoice when work is already delivered and should be billed now.

- Required: `request_id`, `name`, `total`, `billing_mode`
- Optional: `business_id`, `client_id`, `client_name`, `currency`, `entries`, `installments`, `start_now`, `starts_on`, `target_end`, `notes`, `source_estimate_id`

### `update_engagement`

*Update Engagement*, needs **write**.

Correct the details around an engagement: its name, the dates it runs between, or its internal notes. Fields left out are kept as they are. The agreed total, the currency, the billing mode and the schedule are deliberately not editable here, because changing an agreed number after work has been billed against it is a renegotiation rather than an edit. Nothing is sent to anyone.

- Required: `request_id`, `engagement_id`
- Optional: `name`, `starts_on`, `target_end`, `notes`

### `mark_milestone_complete`

*Mark Milestone Complete*, needs **write**.

Record that a schedule entry has been delivered. An entry waiting on a milestone becomes ready to bill; an entry waiting on the start or the end of the engagement, or on a date, keeps its own rule and is simply stamped complete. Nothing is invoiced and nothing is sent: use list_ready_to_bill to see what this freed up, then raise an invoice for it.

- Required: `request_id`, `entry_id`
- Optional: nothing

### `complete_engagement`

*Complete Engagement*, needs **write**.

Close out an engagement: the work is finished. Every schedule entry waiting on completion becomes ready to bill, and if any money is left unbilled the answer says how much, so nothing is quietly forgotten. Completing does not invoice anything and does not send anything. A completed engagement cannot be reopened, so do this when the work really is done.

- Required: `request_id`, `engagement_id`
- Optional: nothing

### `waive_engagement_entry`

*Waive Engagement Entry*, needs **write**.

Write off a schedule entry that will not be charged, with a reason. The entry stays in the schedule so the agreement still reads the way it was agreed, but it stops counting towards what is left to bill. Use this when part of the work was dropped or absorbed. An entry that has already been invoiced cannot be waived: that is a credit note, and it belongs on the invoice. Nothing is sent to anyone.

- Required: `request_id`, `entry_id`, `reason`
- Optional: nothing

### `convert_estimate_to_engagement`

*Convert Estimate to Engagement*, needs **write**.

Turn an accepted estimate into an engagement: the same client, the same total and the same currency, now with a payment schedule instead of a single bill. Use this when the quote was agreed but the work will be billed in parts, and convert_estimate_to_invoice when the whole amount is due at once. An estimate can become one or the other, never both, so this refuses a quote that already became an invoice or an engagement. The engagement is created as a draft and nothing is billed or sent: start it when the work begins, which is what makes any deposit ready to bill.

- Required: `request_id`, `estimate_id`, `billing_mode`
- Optional: `entries`, `installments`

## Saved items

The rate catalog invoices and estimates can bill from by name.

| Tool | Needs | Required input |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `list_items` | read | none |
| `create_item` | write | `name`, `rate` |
| `update_item` | write | none |

### `list_items`

*List Saved Items*, needs **read**.

List the saved product/service catalog for a business, with each item's stored rate. Use this before create_invoice or create_estimate when the user names a service ("Consulting", "Design retainer") so you bill the saved rate instead of guessing. Not for looking up what was billed on a specific invoice; use get_invoice for that.

- Required: nothing
- Optional: `offset`, `business_id`, `search`, `include_inactive`, `limit`

### `create_item`

*Create Saved Item*, needs **write**.

Add a product or service to the saved catalog so future invoices and estimates can bill it by name at a consistent rate. Use this when the user says "my rate for X is Y" or wants a reusable line. Do NOT use it to add a one-off line to an existing invoice; pass line_items to create_invoice or update_draft_invoice instead.

- Required: `name`, `rate`
- Optional: `business_id`, `description`, `unit`, `type`, `tax_rate`

### `update_item`

*Update Saved Item*, needs **write**.

Change a saved item's rate, name, description, unit, or active flag. Identify it by item_id or by exact item_name. Changes apply to FUTURE invoices and estimates only; already-issued documents keep the rate they were billed at, so do not use this to correct an invoice (use update_draft_invoice).

- Required: nothing
- Optional: `business_id`, `item_id`, `item_name`, `name`, `rate`, `description`, `unit`, `type`, `tax_rate`, `is_active`

## Time

Log and correct tracked time before it gets billed.

| Tool | Needs | Required input |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `log_time` | write | `request_id`, `description`, `hours` |
| `list_time_entries` | read | none |
| `update_time_entry` | write | `time_entry_id` |
| `delete_time_entry` | delete | `time_entry_id` |

### `log_time`

*Log Time*, needs **write**.

Log a time entry for a client, identified by client_id or client_name (exact match, case-insensitive). Billable by default.

- Required: `request_id`, `description`, `hours`
- Optional: `business_id`, `client_id`, `client_name`, `date`, `rate`, `billable`

### `list_time_entries`

*List Time Entries*, needs **read**.

List tracked time, filtered by client, date range, and billed status. Use this to answer "how many hours did I put into X" or to find the entry to correct. To draft an invoice from unbilled work, prefer list_unbilled, which groups by client and totals it for you.

- Required: nothing
- Optional: `offset`, `business_id`, `client_id`, `client_name`, `from`, `to`, `billed`, `billable`, `limit`

### `update_time_entry`

*Update Time Entry*, needs **write**.

Correct a single logged time entry: its hours, rate, description, date, client, or billable flag. Use it to fix a mistake before the work is invoiced. Refuses entries already attached to an invoice, since changing those would not change the invoice the client received.

- Required: `time_entry_id`
- Optional: `description`, `hours`, `date`, `rate`, `client_id`, `client_name`, `billable`

### `delete_time_entry`

*Delete Time Entry*, needs **delete (removes a record)**.

Permanently delete ONE time entry by its id, returning what was deleted so it can be re-logged if that was a mistake. There is no bulk delete and no filter-based delete on purpose. Refuses entries already attached to an invoice. Prefer update_time_entry when the entry is merely wrong rather than unwanted.

- Required: `time_entry_id`
- Optional: nothing

## Expenses

Log and correct expenses, billable or not.

| Tool | Needs | Required input |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `log_expense` | write | `request_id`, `description`, `amount` |
| `list_expenses` | read | none |
| `update_expense` | write | `expense_id` |
| `delete_expense` | delete | `expense_id` |

### `log_expense`

*Log Expense*, needs **write**.

Log a business expense. A client is optional; identify one by client_id or client_name (exact match, case-insensitive) to attach the expense for later billing.

- Required: `request_id`, `description`, `amount`
- Optional: `business_id`, `client_id`, `client_name`, `date`, `category`, `billable`

### `list_expenses`

*List Expenses*, needs **read**.

List expenses filtered by category, client, date range, and billed status, with totals grouped per currency. Use this for "what did I spend on software last quarter" or to find an expense to correct. For rebilling unbilled costs to a client, prefer list_unbilled.

- Required: nothing
- Optional: `offset`, `business_id`, `category`, `client_id`, `client_name`, `from`, `to`, `billed`, `billable`, `limit`

### `update_expense`

*Update Expense*, needs **write**.

Correct a single logged expense: amount, description, vendor, category, date, client, or billable flag. Use it to fix a mistake before the cost is rebilled. Refuses expenses already attached to an invoice, since changing those would not change the invoice the client received.

- Required: `expense_id`
- Optional: `description`, `amount`, `date`, `category`, `vendor`, `notes`, `client_id`, `client_name`, `billable`

### `delete_expense`

*Delete Expense*, needs **delete (removes a record)**.

Permanently delete ONE expense by its id, returning what was deleted so it can be re-logged if that was a mistake. There is no bulk delete and no filter-based delete on purpose. Refuses expenses already attached to an invoice. Prefer update_expense when the expense is merely wrong rather than unwanted.

- Required: `expense_id`
- Optional: nothing

## Payments

Check what has been paid, what is still due, and correct or void a payment that was recorded wrong.

| Tool | Needs | Required input |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `get_payment_status` | read | `invoice_id` |
| `update_payment` | payments | `request_id`, `payment_id` |
| `void_payment` | payments | `request_id`, `payment_id`, `reason` |

### `get_payment_status`

*Get Payment Status*, needs **read**.

Report where one invoice stands on money: amount due, amount paid, each recorded payment with its payment_id, whether online card payment is switched on, and the link a client can pay from. Use it to answer "has X paid yet" or "what do they still owe". Voided payments are left out of the list and every total unless include_voided is true. Read-only: use record_payment to log a payment that came in outside Stripe, update_payment to correct one, and void_payment to undo one.

- Required: `invoice_id`
- Optional: `include_voided`

### `update_payment`

*Update Payment*, needs **payments (moves recorded money)**.

Correct a recorded payment: the date it landed, the method, the reference number, the notes, or the amount if a figure was keyed wrong. The invoice is recomputed from its live payments, so a smaller amount reopens a balance and moves a paid invoice back to partial. Use this to fix a payment whose date was recorded wrong, which otherwise puts the money in the wrong month of every revenue report. Payments collected through Stripe cannot be edited: a card payment is changed by issuing a refund in Stripe, which arrives back here as its own ledger entry. Fields left out are kept as they are.

- Required: `request_id`, `payment_id`
- Optional: `payment_date`, `method`, `notes`, `reference_number`, `amount`

### `void_payment`

*Void Payment*, needs **payments (moves recorded money)**.

Void a payment that should never have been recorded, with a reason. The row is kept and stays visible, struck through with its reason, but it stops counting as money: the invoice reopens for that amount and every total, report and list leaves it out. Use this for a payment entered twice, entered against the wrong invoice, or entered for money that never arrived. Payments collected through Stripe cannot be voided: refund the charge in Stripe instead, and the refund arrives back here as its own ledger entry.

- Required: `request_id`, `payment_id`, `reason`
- Optional: nothing

## Business and links

Business settings, revenue rollups, and shareable links.

| Tool | Needs | Required input |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `get_profile` | read | none |
| `get_business` | read | none |
| `list_businesses` | read | none |
| `revenue_summary` | read | none |
| `get_invoice_link` | read | `invoice_id` |
| `list_unbilled` | read | none |

### `get_profile`

*Get Profile*, needs **read**.

Return the Billr account this connection signs in as: a stable opaque id, the name and the email address. Use it to confirm which Billr login is connected; use list_businesses for the businesses it can act on.

- Required: nothing
- Optional: nothing

### `get_business`

*Get Business*, needs **read**.

Fetch details for one of the caller's businesses: name, contact email, currency, invoice numbering. If the API key is scoped to a single business, business_id can be omitted.

- Required: nothing
- Optional: `business_id`

### `list_businesses`

*List Businesses*, needs **read**.

List every business this API key can act on, ordered by name. Call this first when you don't know which business_id to pass to the other tools. If exactly one is returned, business_id can be omitted everywhere.

- Required: nothing
- Optional: nothing

### `revenue_summary`

*Revenue Summary*, needs **read**.

Summarize invoiced, paid, outstanding, and overdue amounts for one of the caller's businesses over a period (default this_year), plus status counts and the top 5 clients by invoiced amount. Draft and cancelled invoices are excluded from all dollar totals (but still counted in by_status); "overdue" means balance still due, due date past, and status is sent/viewed/partial; overdue_total is a subset of outstanding_total, not additional to it.

- Required: nothing
- Optional: `business_id`, `period`

### `get_invoice_link`

*Get Invoice Link*, needs **read**.

Get the shareable public link and PDF download link for an invoice. The invoice must belong to one of the caller's businesses.

- Required: `invoice_id`
- Optional: nothing

### `list_unbilled`

*List Unbilled Work*, needs **read**.

List billable time entries and expenses not yet attached to an invoice, grouped by client with totals. Use this to draft an invoice from a client's unbilled work; entries missing an hourly rate are flagged. Billable entries with no client can't be grouped into a client invoice, so they're excluded from `clients` but still surfaced via the summary and the `unassigned` field.

- Required: nothing
- Optional: `offset`, `business_id`, `client_id`
